By starting with manual report generation in 3 cities where ADU regulations recently changed (ensuring high search volume and homeowner confusion), LotReady validates demand at $149/report with minimal upfront engineering cost. The $499 Concierge tier captures higher willingness-to-pay from serious buyers while creating a referral revenue stream from architects and contractors. The phased approach — hand-aggregate zoning data, use Airtable/Zapier for automation, then build a proper platform — keeps burn rate near zero while proving unit economics. Once patterns stabilize across initial cities, the zoning logic engine becomes the defensible moat, and expansion to new municipalities becomes incremental data work rather than product rebuilds. The competitive landscape is fragmented (no dominant player surfaced), giving LotReady a first-mover window to own SEO for 'ADU feasibility' queries city by city.

**Niche:** ADU feasibility analysis for residential homeowners navigating complex zoning and permitting requirements
**ICP:** Homeowners aged 35-65 in high-cost metro areas (Los Angeles, San Jose, Portland, Seattle) who are considering building an ADU for rental income, multigenerational living, or property value appreciation, and who want clarity on feasibility before committing $5K+ to an architect or consultant.

## Strategy
This strategy exploits a clear information asymmetry: homeowners currently pay $5K+ to architects for feasibility opinions that can be largely automated with publicly available parcel and zoning data. By starting with manual report generation in 3 cities where ADU regulations recently changed (ensuring high search volume and homeowner confusion), LotReady validates demand at $149/report with minimal upfront engineering cost. The free Quick Check serves as a high-conversion lead magnet — homeowners enter their address, get a teaser result, and are motivated to purchase the full report. The $499 Concierge tier captures higher willingness-to-pay from serious buyers while creating a referral revenue stream from architects and contractors. The phased approach — hand-aggregate zoning data, use Airtable/Zapier for automation, then build a proper platform — keeps burn rate near zero while proving unit economics. Once patterns stabilize across initial cities, the zoning logic engine becomes the defensible moat, and expansion to new municipalities becomes incremental data work rather than product rebuilds. The competitive landscape is fragmented (no dominant player surfaced), giving LotReady a first-mover window to own SEO for 'ADU feasibility' queries city by city.
